Assessment expiry

Schedule verified agent removal at a specific time. At expiry, each online device removes the Patched uploader and service. Local Patched credentials, queued uploads and cached artefacts are removed only if you explicitly select the purge option below. Server-side tenant records are retained.

Danger zone
Offboard customer

Marks this tenant inactive and revokes agent access immediately. All data is preserved and the tenant can be restored from the Offboarded view. This does not remove Patched agents or locally cached Patched data from devices.

Remove Patched agents

Sends a separately audited immediate removal directive to every registered device. This is not part of customer offboarding and does not delete server-side tenant records.

Permanently delete (purge)

Hard-deletes all devices, compliance data, app inventory and raw payloads. Cannot be undone. Available once the tenant is offboarded — purge from the Offboarded customers list.

Customer Access

Emails authorised to sign in to this tenant's customer portal. Access is checked at login via Cloudflare Access — granting access here does not send any email; it only authorises an email that already has (or will separately be given, as a manual out-of-band step) a Cloudflare Access identity in Patched's directory. Once both steps are done, Send welcome emails that person their sign-in instructions. It is refused unless their exact address is verified live against the app.patched.im Cloudflare Access Allow policy first.

Grant portal access

Authorises an email to sign in to this tenant's customer portal. This does not send an email or create any account by itself — the person still needs a Cloudflare Access identity in Patched's directory (a separate, manual step) before they can actually sign in.

Named individuals only. Sign-in is a one-time PIN sent to the address itself, so access is personal to whoever holds that mailbox. Role and shared addresses (it@, admin@, support@, info@, helpdesk@, security@, office@, accounts@, team@, all@) are refused when you send the welcome email.

This paragraph is the product. It is what makes the document usable by an assessor and it is what nobody else hands the customer.

Once issued, it does not change
The numbers are frozen at the moment of issue, and the coverage figure is stored with them, so a later improvement never rewrites history.
A content hash is printed on the document, so a customer can prove the copy their assessor holds is the copy that was issued.
A correction is a new report that supersedes the old one, never an edit. Both stay in the list.

Deploy agent

Generate a single-use enrollment token for this tenant and download the deployment artifact.
Generating token…
Path 1 — MDM (preferred)

Generate a single-use, 24-hour enrollment token and download the ready-to-deploy artifact for your MDM. The token is consumed on first agent contact — regenerate if unused after 24 hours.

macOS — Intune Platform Script

Upload as an Intune Platform Script (shell, run as root). Writes the enrollment token to /etc/patched/enrollment-token on the device before the agent runs.

Windows — MSI command

Run via Intune Win32 app detection or paste into your RMM install command.

Token expires:  ·  Token ID:

Path 2: Stamped installer link Coming soon

Bundle-stamped macOS tarball + Windows MSI with the enrollment token pre-baked. Mint a signed 48-hour download link and optionally email it to the customer. Available once the agent signing and bundle-stamping pipeline is complete.

Offboard tenant

The tenant's agents will be blocked from ingesting immediately. All data is preserved and the tenant can be restored from the Offboarded view. This does not remove the agent software or locally cached Patched data.

If agent removal is required, cancel this offboard action and complete the separate Remove Patched agents step first. That step refreshes the exact device count, requires the tenant name again and tracks each device outcome. Offboarding can block devices from collecting a removal directive, so do not treat this action as a shortcut.

Type to confirm:

Remove Patched agents

This sends an immediate removal directive to exactly 0 devices. Each device must acknowledge the signed directive before acting, then report whether removal succeeded.

The command removes the Patched uploader and service. Local Patched credentials, queued uploads and cached artefacts are removed only if you explicitly select the purge option below. It does not delete the tenant or its server-side history. Offline devices remain pending until they next check in; the Console does not claim success until a device reports it.

Type to confirm:

Permanently delete tenant

This cannot be undone. All devices, compliance data, app inventory, and raw payloads will be permanently deleted.
